briefing.intro: We are OSDC. We build things, break things, ship weird ideas, help each other improve, and leave enough behind for the next batch to keep going.

agenda.task: Make the poster loud enough to stop a hallway scroll
Get new people from 'I just joined' to 'I can ship one thing'
Open sprint, pairing tables, repo triage, no spectator mode
Archive screenshots, notes, and all the lessons future us will forget

focus: Keep OSDC beginner-friendly without turning it into tutorial soup
Make open source feel like something members can enter this week, not next year
Leave enough lore in the archive for the next core team to continue the bit

events.intro: Our events are build spaces. Hackathons, jams, CTFs, workshops, demo nights, and occasional controlled chaos.

items.title: OSDHack // Build Sprint
items.description: A club-wide shipping sprint with mentor tables, fast feedback loops, and enough energy drinks to concern the ops desk.

items.title: CodeJam // Capture The Flag
items.description: Challenge blocks, exploit walkthroughs, and post-round writeups so newcomers leave smarter, not just confused louder.

items.title: Maintainer Night
items.description: Lightning talks, live triage, and the path from 'first PR merged' to 'wait why am I responsible for this repo now'.

members.intro: We work best when people do not stay passive for long. Join, pick a lane, get context, ship something, then help the next person do the same.

squads.focus: Club site, experiments, event tooling, and whatever repo someone bravely opened
Poster systems, motion, UI accents, and making chaos readable
squads.next: Approve the OSDHack poster before someone adds another glow layer

squads.focus: Onboarding, pairing, member spotlights, and making newcomers feel expected
squads.next: Run the onboarding desk and route people into real work

squads.focus: Venue wrangling, archive capture, volunteer logistics, and preventing preventable fire
squads.next: Lock demo recording workflow before demo night becomes lost media

board: Beginners are welcome, but not sentenced to spectator mode
Every sprint should leave behind something reusable: code, docs, posters, or lore
Lane changes are allowed; the only banned state is permanent hesitation

alumni.intro: Our alumni are how knowledge survives handoffs, how review loops stay honest, and how newer members see what comes next.

officeHours.focus: Portfolio review, internship prep, contribution path, and mild reality checks
Platform engineering, Linux, tooling, OSS careers, and one inevitable package-manager rant
Poster critiques, storytelling, interface direction, and stopping us from centering everything

outcomes: Mentors review event pages before launch so the main team does not disappear into its own tunnel vision
Guest maintainers help newer members understand not just what to build, but how to contribute responsibly
Legacy repos stay documented so good work does not die with graduating seniors

pastEvents.intro: Archive log. We keep receipts: what shipped, what flopped, what people loved, and what should never again be scheduled five minutes before a quiz.

archive.title: Spring Open Sprint
archive.note: Small teams plus a public task board beat heroic solo grinding

archive.title: Poster-led Demo Night
archive.note: Ridiculously loud posters worked. regrettably, the internet was right

archive.title: Maintainer Loop Session
archive.note: Live triage turned vague interest into actual first issues

repeat: Make the weird idea legible, not sterile
Always pair hype with a concrete next step
Archive the screenshots the same night or accept that they are gone forever
